## Assistant

Short answer: **discovery only answers “is Claude/Codex installed?”** — it does **not** make an agent *run as* Claude or Codex. That choice is a separate **runtime pin**, and Buzz and Agensis do it very differently.

---

## How Buzz does it (desktop owns the process)

Buzz is a **local agent host**. The desktop app itself spawns Claude/Codex as child processes.

```
UI: pick harness (Claude / Codex / Amp / Grok / …)
        ↓
agent record.runtime = "codex"   (or persona.runtime)
        ↓
desktop resolves binary (discover PATH)
        ↓
spawn: codex-acp / claude-agent-acp / amp-acp / grok …
        ↓
talk over ACP (stdio JSON-RPC)  ← Buzz speaks ACP, not `claude -p`
```

Important Buzz details:

| Piece | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Harness catalog** | Discovered CLIs (what we just ported the *probe* side of) |
| **Agent/persona `runtime`** | Which harness this agent uses |
| **Spawn** | Desktop main process runs the binary |
| **Wire protocol** | **ACP** (Agent Client Protocol) — adapters like `claude-agent-acp`, `codex-acp` |
| **Auth** | Your existing `claude` / `codex login` on that Mac |

So in Buzz, “speak to Codex” = **this agent’s harness is Codex → spawn Codex’s ACP adapter**.

---

## How Agensis does it today (daemon on the wire)

Agensis does **not** spawn Claude/Codex inside Electron. The web/desktop UI talks to the **backend**; the backend talks to a **daemon** over WebSocket; the daemon is what runs Claude/Codex/Amp on the machine where it was started.

```
UI: agent run_mode = "daemon"
    agent.metadata.runtime = "claude" | "codex" | "amp"
        ↓
Generate connect command (stamps --runtime)
        ↓
You run on a machine:
  agensis connect --runtime codex --url … --token aga_… --agent …
        ↓
Daemon connects over WS, reports capabilities.runtimes
        ↓
@agent in channel → server enqueues agent_job → daemon runs
  claude SDK / codex app-server / amp
```

### How you specify runtime in Agensis UI

1. **Agents** window → create/edit agent  
2. Location: **Remote** (daemon), not Built-in  
3. Runtime select: **Claude / Codex / Amp**  
4. That writes `metadata.runtime` on the agent row  
5. **Generate connect command** — the server puts that into the shell line:

```bash
agensis connect --runtime codex --url https://… --token aga_… --agent <id> …
```

(from `agentConnectionCommand` in `server/index.cjs` — `--runtime` only if pinned)

6. Run that command on the machine that has Codex/Claude installed  
7. Daemon must declare the same runtime; server enforces it (`assertMatchingExecutionRuntime` / disconnect on mismatch)

### How the daemon “speaks” to each runtime

| Runtime | What the daemon actually runs |
|---|---|
| **Claude** | Claude Agent SDK (`query()` → still uses local `claude` CLI) or `claude -p` fallback |
| **Codex** | `codex app-server` (JSON-RPC stdio pool) or `codex exec` fallback |
| **Amp** | `amp` CLI path (`ampRuntime.mjs`) |
| **Grok** | **Not an execution runtime today** — only detected as a CLI in Tools |

Grok is in discovery for “installed tools”; it is **not** in `AgentExecutionRuntime = 'claude' | 'codex' | 'amp'`.

### Built-in vs Remote

| Mode | Who runs the turn |
|---|---|
| **Built-in** | Server (Fly) with Anthropic API key — no local Claude/Codex |
| **Remote (daemon)** | Your machine’s `agensis connect` process using local CLIs |

So: **specifying Claude vs Codex is the agent’s runtime + the connect command’s `--runtime`, not Settings → Tools.**

---

## How the pieces relate (including what we just added)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Settings → Tools  (what we baked into Electron)        │
│  “Is claude/codex/amp/grok on THIS Mac?”                │
│  Does NOT spawn jobs. Status only.                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Agents → Remote + runtime Claude/Codex/Amp             │
│  metadata.runtime = pin                                 │
│  Connect command includes --runtime                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  agensis connect (separate process, still required)     │
│  Speaks to Claude/Codex/Amp on the host                 │
│  Reports capabilities.runtimes back to server           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The Agents UI already uses **daemon-reported** runtimes for “Claude — ready / not installed”, not the new desktop discovery:

```300:313:src/components/windows/AgentsWindowContent.tsx
function runtimeChoiceNote(choice: AgentRuntimeChoice): string {
  if (choice.available === true) return 'ready';
  if (choice.available === null) return 'not reported by a connected daemon';
  // ...
}
```

So today:

- **Discovery** = “this Mac has the CLI” (Tools panel)  
- **Runtime pin** = “this agent must use Codex”  
- **Speaking** = daemon with matching `--runtime` actually running  

---

## Practical “I want this agent to use Codex”

1. Install + log in: `codex` on the Mac  
2. Agents → agent → **Remote** → runtime **Codex** → Save  
3. **Generate connect command**  
4. Run it in a terminal (or keep it as a launchd service)  
5. Agent shows Connected; @mention it in a channel  

Same for Claude with runtime **Claude**. Amp needs Amp signed in (`amp login`).

If you switch Claude → Codex on a connected agent, the server **kicks the old daemon** and you must reconnect with a new command that has `--runtime codex`.

---

## Buzz vs Agensis (the real architectural gap)

| | **Buzz** | **Agensis (today)** |
|---|---|---|
| Where Claude/Codex run | Inside desktop process | Separate `agensis connect` daemon |
| Protocol | ACP adapters | Daemon WS + SDK / app-server / amp CLI |
| Specifying runtime | Agent/persona harness field | `metadata.runtime` + connect `--runtime` |
| Desktop discovery | Feeds the spawn list | Feeds Tools status only (for now) |
| “Start agent” in UI | Spawns local process | Mints command for you to run |

So: **Buzz speaks to Codex by spawning it. Agensis speaks to Codex by a connected daemon that was started with `--runtime codex`.**

---

## What is *not* wired yet

Desktop discovery does **not** yet:

1. Fill the agent runtime dropdown from local installs (still “not reported by a connected daemon” until a daemon is up)  
2. Auto-spawn `agensis connect` when you pick Codex  
3. Talk ACP like Buzz (no in-app spawn of `claude` / `codex`)  
4. Treat Grok as a job runtime  

That would be the next product step if you want Buzz-like “pick Codex → it just runs here” without a manual connect command.

If you want that path, the cleanest versions are roughly:

- **A. Desktop sidecar** — Electron starts/supervises `agensis connect` for agents pinned to local runtimes (reuses existing protocol)  
- **B. Full Buzz-style ACP** — desktop speaks ACP itself (bigger rewrite, different wire path)

**A** matches current Agensis; **B** matches Buzz’s model more closely.

I can sketch or implement **A** (local discovery → auto-connect daemons for agents with `metadata.runtime`) if that’s the direction you want.

## Assistant

Here’s a concrete desktop-only design that feels like Buzz, speaks real ACP, and doesn’t break the existing web/daemon product.

## What “smooth like Buzz” actually is

Buzz is not “detect CLI → run shell command.” It’s three layers:

| Layer | Buzz | Agensis today |
|---|---|---|
| **Discover** | PATH + common dirs + login shell | We just added this (partial) |
| **Host** | Desktop **spawns** harnesses as children | User must run `agensis connect` by hand |
| **Talk** | **ACP over stdio** (JSON-RPC) | Claude SDK / codex app-server / amp CLI |

Buzz’s actual spawn path:

```
Desktop → spawn buzz-acp (or adapter)
            → ACP stdio → claude-agent-acp | codex-acp | amp-acp | grok …
            → agent uses tools on disk
            ← stream updates back into Buzz UI / relay
```

ACP is the LSP for coding agents: one client protocol, many agents.

---

## Target shape for Agensis desktop

**New role: Desktop Agent Host** — Electron main is an **ACP client** and the process owner. The renderer never spawns agents; it only picks harness + starts/stops.

```
┌─ Renderer (React) ─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Agents: harness = Codex · "Running on this Mac"       │
│  Channel @mention / job UI (same as today)             │
└────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
             │ IPC (start/stop/turn/status)
┌────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Electron main — Desktop Agent Host                    │
│  · discovery (done)                                    │
│  · harness catalog + install hints                     │
│  · ACP session pool (per agent, optionally per thread) │
│  · maps agensis job ↔ ACP session/prompt/update        │
└────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
             │ spawn + stdio JSON-RPC (ACP)
┌────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  claude-agent-acp │ codex-acp │ amp-acp │ grok │ …     │
│  (vendor login already on machine)                     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
             ▲
             │ turns still authorized by backend
┌────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Backend (local or Fly): messages, RBAC, agent_jobs    │
│  Desktop claims jobs for agents marked local-acp       │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Critical product rule:**  
Web stays on **daemon** (`agensis connect`).  
Desktop gets a second execution mode: **local ACP**.  
Same agent identity / channels / RBAC; different *how the turn runs*.

---

## How you “specify Claude vs Codex” (UX)

Same mental model as Buzz’s harness picker:

1. Create agent (or open existing).
2. **Location: This Mac** (desktop-only; not Built-in, not “Remote daemon”).
3. **Harness:** Claude Code / Codex / Amp / Grok / …  
   - List built from discovery  
   - Greys out missing / AdapterMissing  
   - One-click install hint (npm global adapter, like Buzz)
4. Click **Start** → host spawns ACP adapter; no copy-paste connect command.
5. Agent shows **Connected · Codex · this Mac**.
6. @mention in a channel → job lands on desktop host → ACP turn → stream into message (same UX as daemon turns).

Storage (fits existing columns, no new security surface):

```ts
run_mode: 'local-acp'          // or keep 'daemon' + metadata.execution = 'acp'
metadata: {
  harness: 'codex',            // catalog id
  // optional: model, cwd override, adapter path pin
}
```

Server rule: only a **desktop host** for that agent may claim those jobs (token / connection kind), same spirit as today’s runtime mismatch kick.

---

## How we “speak” ACP (protocol map)

ACP is client ↔ agent over **stdio** (or HTTP). Client owns the editor environment; agent thinks and runs tools.

Rough mapping for Agensis:

| Agensis concept | ACP concept |
|---|---|
| Agent online on desktop | Spawned process + `initialize` |
| First job / thread open | `session/new` (cwd = workspace `local_path`) |
| Dispatch / @mention | `session/prompt` with fenced channel context |
| Streaming “Thinking…” / tokens | `session/update` → UPDATE message content (existing fanout) |
| Tool approval UI | ACP permission requests → your existing permission cards |
| Cancel job | ACP cancel / kill session |
| Stop agent | Kill process, mark offline |

You do **not** need Buzz’s Nostr/relay/buzz-acp harness. Their `buzz-acp` exists because Buzz’s network is a relay. **Your network is already `agent_jobs` + WebSocket.** The desktop host is the thin ACP client *and* the job worker.

Harness catalog (Buzz-aligned):

| id | Underlying CLI | ACP entry |
|---|---|---|
| claude | `claude` | `claude-agent-acp` / `claude-code-acp` |
| codex | `codex` | `codex-acp` |
| amp | `amp` | `amp-acp` |
| grok | `grok` | `grok agent … stdio` (if they ship ACP mode) |
| cursor / opencode / kimi / … | vendor | their ACP flags |

Discovery you started becomes the **catalog**; spawn uses **adapter path first**, then underlying CLI for auth/login probes.

---

## Smoothness checklist (what makes it feel like Buzz)

1. **Zero terminal for the happy path** — Start/Stop in UI.  
2. **Harness picker shows real availability** — Available / Adapter missing / CLI missing / Login needed.  
3. **Rescan after install** — already sketched (login-shell PATH cache).  
4. **Warm sessions** — one ACP process per agent (or per agent+thread), not spawn-per-message.  
5. **CWD** — workspace project folder (`local_path`) as default ACP workspace.  
6. **Permissions** — map ACP approvals onto existing `agent_permission_requests` so UX stays one system.  
7. **Stop reasons** — map ACP end reasons into your closed `STOP_REASONS` set.  
8. **No secret in UI** — still use short-lived connect/host tokens; never show vendor API keys.

---

## Architecture choice (recommend this)

### Recommended: **Desktop Host as job worker + ACP client**

```
@agent message
  → backend creates agent_job (unchanged)
  → desktop host (WS or local backend) claims job
  → ACP session/prompt
  → stream UPDATE into messages
  → job done
```

**Why this over pure “renderer talks ACP”:**  
RBAC, private sessions, fanout, audit stay on the server. Desktop only replaces the *executor*, not the control plane.

**Why this over “wrap agensis connect in Electron”:**  
That stays on Claude-SDK / app-server / amp paths, not ACP, and you keep fighting per-vendor protocols. ACP is the long-term multi-agent surface (Claude, Codex, Amp, Grok, Cursor, …).

**Why not full Buzz clone (buzz-acp + relay):**  
You already have identity, channels, jobs, and realtime. Rebuilding a Nostr harness is wasted surface area.

---

## Phased plan (desktop-only, shippable)

### Phase 0 — Catalog (mostly done)
- Discovery of CLI + **adapter** binaries  
- Status: Available / AdapterMissing / NotInstalled / Auth  
- Settings → Tools already useful

### Phase 1 — ACP client in Electron main
- Small module: `electron/acp-host.cjs`  
  - spawn adapter with login-shell PATH  
  - JSON-RPC framing  
  - `initialize` / `session/new` / `session/prompt` / cancel  
- Unit-test against a fake ACP process (no real Claude required)

### Phase 2 — Agent lifecycle UI
- `run_mode: local-acp` (or desktop flag)  
- Harness select from catalog  
- Start / Stop / Restart on this Mac  
- Connection row: `host: 'desktop'`, capabilities from discovery + live process

### Phase 3 — Job bridge
- Desktop claims `agent_jobs` for local-acp agents  
- Stream into existing message UPDATE path  
- Permission + cancel hooks

### Phase 4 — Polish
- Auto-start last running agents on app launch  
- Install adapter from UI (`npm i -g @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp`)  
- Grok / Cursor / OpenCode as catalog entries  
- Doctor panel: path, version, login, adapter min version (Buzz’s codex-acp floor)

### Explicit non-goals for v1
- Replacing Fly daemon for **web** users  
- ACP on Netlify/server (no user laptop FS)  
- Replacing `agensis-agent` overnight (keep daemon for remote machines)

---

## How this coexists with current daemon agents

| Mode | Who runs code | Protocol |
|---|---|---|
| Built-in | Server API keys | Anthropic API |
| Remote daemon | `agensis connect` on any machine | today’s WS + SDK/app-server |
| **This Mac (new)** | Electron host | **ACP stdio** |

Same `@agent`, same channels. Only the execution lane changes.

There’s already a partial ACP thread in `agensis-agent` (CLI `--acp-arg --stdio` parser issues in `status.md`). Prefer **desktop-owned ACP client** over finishing that as the only path — the smooth product is “app hosts agents,” not “user pastes another flag.”

---

## Implementation sketch (where code lives)

```
electron/
  main.cjs                 # IPC: harnesses, start, stop, job claim hooks
  acp/
    host.cjs               # process pool
    client.cjs             # JSON-RPC ACP client
    harnesses.cjs          # catalog ids → command/args (Buzz table)
    jobBridge.cjs          # agent_jobs ↔ ACP turns
shared/
  local-agent-discovery.cjs  # already: resolve paths
  harness-catalog.cjs        # pure catalog (testable)
src/
  components/.../Agents…   # This Mac + harness picker + Start
```

IPC surface (minimal):

```ts
electronAPI.localAgents.list()           // discovery catalog
electronAPI.localAgents.start(agentId)   // spawn ACP for agent’s harness
electronAPI.localAgents.stop(agentId)
electronAPI.localAgents.status(agentId)
// turns: either host pulls jobs via existing WS, or main registers as daemon-shaped client
```

**Auth trick that keeps UX smooth:** desktop host authenticates to the backend as a **special local connection** (minted once when user clicks Start, stored in Electron safeStorage) — same idea as connect token, but the app holds it, not a terminal.

---

## Risks (be honest)

1. **ACP adapter quality varies** — Codex/Claude adapters change; pin min versions (Buzz does this for codex-acp).  
2. **Permissions model** — ACP tool approval ≠ your current `canUseTool` / metadata rules; map carefully or fail closed.  
3. **Streaming fidelity** — map ACP events to your message stream so the UI doesn’t feel worse than daemon.  
4. **Two executors** — don’t let daemon + local-acp both claim the same agent; one live host invariant.  
5. **Packaged Electron PATH** — you already need login-shell PATH (done for discovery); spawn must use the same.

---

## Bottom line

To feel like Buzz **and** use ACP:

1. **Desktop is the host** (spawn + lifecycle).  
2. **ACP is the only local execution protocol** for that mode.  
3. **Backend stays control plane** (jobs, RBAC, messages).  
4. **User specifies harness on the agent** and hits **Start** — no `agensis connect` for desktop-local.

Discovery is step 0. The missing product is the **ACP session pool + Start/Stop + job bridge**.

If you want to proceed, I’d implement in this order:  
**Phase 1 client + fake ACP tests → Phase 2 Start/Stop UI for one harness (Codex) → Phase 3 one end-to-end channel turn → then Claude/Amp/Grok.**

Say if you want that as a written design doc in-repo or to start Phase 1 in the Electron tree.

## What you get

**Electron owns the agent process** (Buzz-style). No terminal for the happy path.

```
Agents → Connect → Start on this Mac (ACP)
  → pick harness (Grok / Claude / Codex / …)
  → Electron spawns ACP stdio child
  → registers as online agent over WebSocket
  → @mention jobs run through ACP
```

## How to try it

1. `npm run desktop:dev` (or your usual Electron entry)
2. Open an agent → **Connect**
3. **Start on this Mac (ACP)** → choose harness (Grok is available on your box; Claude shows if `claude-code-acp` is installed)
4. Agent should go online; message it in a channel

## Tools

## Assistant

**Yes — that is the intended design.** With one important constraint: **same backend**, and **desktop stays open**.

```
Web (browser)  ──HTTP/WS──►  Backend (127.0.0.1:3142 or Fly)
Electron app   ──HTTP/WS──►  same Backend
                     ▲
                     │ agent_register + agent_job
              Desktop ACP host (local process)
                     │
                     ▼
              grok / claude-acp / codex-acp … on THIS machine
```

### What “accessible via the web” means

| Who | What they see |
|---|---|
| **Desktop** | Start ACP → agent online |
| **Web (or any client on that backend)** | Same agent as **Connected**; `@agent` / jobs dispatch to the desktop host |
| **Who runs the tools** | Always the **Mac running Electron** — not the browser, not Fly |

So the web does **not** run ACP itself. It only talks to the server; the server routes work to the desktop session that registered with the agent’s token.

### Requirements for that to work

1. **Same backend** — if Electron registers against `http://127.0.0.1:3142` and the browser hits production Fly, web will not see that local connection.
2. **Desktop stays running** — closing Electron stops ACP and drops the agent offline.
3. **Start path** — **Connect → Start on this Mac (ACP)** (or equivalent IPC), not only pasting `agensis connect --runtime claude` (that’s the old daemon path).
4. **Valid token** — Start mints/uses a connect token and registers over WS; if mint fails, local process may exist but web won’t see “Connected”.

### Two different “local” modes (don’t mix them up)

| Mode | How it starts | Web sees agent? |
|---|---|---|
| **Desktop ACP** (new) | Electron spawns ACP + registers WS | Yes, if same backend |
| **Classic daemon** | `agensis connect …` in a terminal | Yes, same way — different process |

Both are “local executors online.” ACP is the one **inside Electron without a terminal**.

### Bottom line

- **Local:** ACP process on the desktop machine  
- **Reachable from web:** yes, as a normal connected agent on the **shared** backend  
- **Not:** browser runs Claude/Grok, or Fly runs your laptop’s tools  

If the agent never shows Connected on the web while desktop says Running, the usual bug is **backend URL mismatch** (desktop → 3142, web → hosted) or **register/token failed** — not that web can’t use local ACP in principle.

## Assistant

**They stop.** Quitting that desktop app is treated as a full agent shutdown, not “leave them running in the background.”

What their app does on quit (approx.):

1. **Stop every local managed agent** it is tracking  
2. **SIGTERM** the process groups  
3. Wait briefly (~2s)  
4. **SIGKILL** anything still alive  
5. **Sweep orphans** (harness + worker binaries, PID files, dead-instance reaping)  
6. Clear `runtime_pid` / mark last stopped  

So:

| After quit | Result |
|---|---|
| Local agent processes | Killed (not detached daemons) |
| Online / “running on this Mac” | Goes offline |
| In-flight turns | Dropped / incomplete |
| Next launch | Agents are **off** until something starts them again (they often auto-restore if configured, but that’s a new spawn, not continuity) |

Mental model: **desktop = host**. Closing the host ends the agents. Same idea as our Electron ACP path today (`before-quit` → stop bridges + kill ACP children).

They do **not** leave Claude/Codex running as independent services when you quit the app — unless the user separately installed some external always-on agent outside that managed lifecycle.

## Assistant

**Why they flashed online then vanished**

Two real bugs stacked:

### 1. Wrong WebSocket target (main cause)
Desktop **Start on this Mac** used `apiBaseUrl()` → in `desktop:dev` that is **`http://127.0.0.1:5173`** (Vite), not the backend.

So the ACP bridge connected to:

`ws://127.0.0.1:5173/backend/ws` (Vite proxy)

instead of:

`ws://127.0.0.1:3142/backend/ws` (real server)

That can insert an `agent_connections` row (UI: online) and then drop when the proxy/session dies → offline. Matches “there for a second then gone.”

### 2. Runtime pin vs harness
Your connect command was:

`--runtime claude` on agent **Grok Build Web**

Server rule: if `metadata.runtime === 'claude'`, the connection **must** declare `executionRuntime: 'claude'`.  
Starting ACP with harness **Grok** declared nothing / wrong → `runtime_mismatch` → kick.

Also: if **classic `agensis connect` is still running** for the same agent, minting a new token + ACP register **supersedes** the other; they can fight briefly.

---

**Fixes just landed**

| Fix | What it does |
|---|---|
| `resolveHttpBackendBase` | `5173` / `8888` → **`http://127.0.0.1:3142`** |
| Runtime check before connect | Fail clearly if harness ≠ agent pin |
| `agent_disabled` / 1008 | **Stop** reconnect thrash |
| Register → then capabilities | Don’t claim healthy until `agent_registered` |
| UI | Passes `requiredRuntime` from agent metadata; better base URL |

Tests: `desktop-acp-bridge.test.cjs` green (9 total with client tests).

---

**What you should do**

1. **Restart Electron** (`desktop:dev`) so main process loads the new bridge.
2. **Stop** any terminal `agensis connect` for that agent (old token is dead after mint anyway).
3. In Agents → that agent → Connect → **Start on this Mac**:
   - If agent is pinned to **claude**: pick harness **Claude** (needs `claude-code-acp` / `claude-agent-acp`).
   - If you want **Grok**: clear/change the agent’s runtime pin from Claude first (edit agent → runtime), then start with harness Grok.
4. Watch Electron **main** console for:
   - `bridge start … ws=ws://127.0.0.1:3142/backend/ws`
   - `registered agent=…`

If web is on **Fly** while desktop registers on **3142**, they are different worlds — web will never keep a local-only connection. Local web + local backend + fixed bridge should stay online.

## Where you configure it

Saved as:

| UI | Storage |
|---|---|

| Claude / Codex / Amp | `workspace_agents.metadata.runtime` (only when Remote) |

---

## What each mode means

### Built-in
- Runs **on the server** (Fly / local backend).
- Uses **Anthropic API** (workspace vault / env key).
- Model picker = Claude family (`AI_MODELS`: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, …).
- **No** connect command, **no** local CLI, **no** desktop ACP.

### Remote (`daemon`)
- “Someone on a machine will run this agent.”
- Extra control: **runtime** = Claude | Codex | Amp  
  (availability notes come from a **connected daemon’s** `capabilities.runtimes`, not from Electron discovery alone).
- Model depends on runtime:
  - **Claude** → Anthropic list (same as built-in).
  - **Codex** → free text + suggestions (`CODEX_MODELS`); blank = “Codex default” (`auto`).
  - **Amp** → “Amp default” only (Amp picks its own model).
- After save: **Connect** → generate `agensis connect --runtime … --model …` **or** (desktop) **Start on this Mac (ACP)**.

So today, **Remote = “daemon-shaped”**, whether that’s a terminal `agensis connect` or the Electron ACP host. There is **no third location** in the form yet labeled “This Mac”.

---

## How that maps to desktop ACP (current)

| Form setting | Desktop ACP |
|---|---|
| Must be **Remote** | Yes — built-in never uses local ACP |
| **Runtime** Claude/Codex/Amp | Server **pin**: bridge must declare matching `executionRuntime` |
| **Model** | Stored on agent; classic daemon uses it; ACP host only partially wires model (depends on harness) |
| **Connect → Start on this Mac** | Separate control: pick **harness** (Grok, Claude adapter, …) |

Mismatch that bit you earlier:

- Form: Remote + **Claude** + Opus  
- ACP Start: harness **Grok**  
→ server kicks (runtime pin) or wrong executor.

Correct pairings for now:

| Want | Form | Start on this Mac |
|---|---|---|
| Local Claude via ACP | Remote → **Claude** → model | Harness **Claude** |
| Local Codex via ACP | Remote → **Codex** → model | Harness **Codex** |
| Local Amp via ACP | Remote → **Amp** | Harness **Amp** |
| Local Grok via ACP | Remote, **clear/don’t pin Claude**, or no classic runtime pin | Harness **Grok** |

Grok/Hermes/Goose etc. are **not** in the form’s Claude/Codex/Amp select yet — only in the ACP harness list.

```
Form (who/where/what model)
  run_mode + metadata.runtime + model
        │
        ▼
Connect (how it actually comes online)
  • Terminal: agensis connect --runtime …
  • Desktop:  Start on this Mac (ACP harness)
```

Form does **not** yet say “This Mac” or list Grok as a first-class runtime; ACP is bolted onto **Remote** via Connect.

Here’s how **they** configure agents — different shape from our Built-in / Remote / model bar.

## Their model (not “Built-in vs Remote”)

Almost everything local is **on this desktop**. There isn’t a product axis like our “server runs the model” vs “daemon on a laptop.” The axis is:

**Which harness runs the agent on this machine?**

---

## Three layers of config

```
Settings → Harnesses          (what CLIs exist on this Mac)
        ↓
Persona / definition          (who the agent is + preferred harness)
        ↓
Agent instance                (live process: harness + model + provider + Start)
```

### 1. Settings → Harnesses (machine setup)

Catalog from **local discovery** (`discover_acp_providers`):

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Available | Binary found, usable |
| Not installed / adapter missing | Show Install / docs |
| Sign-in needed | CLI present but not logged in |
| Config invalid | Broken config |

Per harness they can: **Install**, **Connect/login**, see path, custom harnesses.  
This is “doctor for local CLIs,” not agent personality.

Global defaults (lowest precedence):

- Default **harness**
- Default **provider** / **model** / env  
  Precedence: floor &lt; **global** &lt; persona &lt; **per-agent**

### 2. Create / edit definition (persona)

Primary control is labeled **“Agent harness”** — not “Claude vs Codex” as abstract runtimes only, but the full catalog:

Claude Code, Codex, Goose, Grok, Cursor, Amp, custom, …

Then, depending on harness:

- **Provider** (when the harness isn’t locked to one vendor)
- **Model** (from runtime/provider capabilities, not one hard-coded Anthropic list)
- Prompt / identity / advanced env

Create can be **definition only** or **definition + start** (`definition_start`): save persona → spawn instance if harness is available.

### 3. Agent instance (running thing)

A **managed agent** is a live local process:

- Tied to a harness (from persona, overridable)
- **Start / Stop / Restart** in the UI (desktop owns the child process)
- Model/provider can be instance overrides
- No “generate connect command and paste in a terminal” as the main path

---

## Create + start (happy path)

1. Open create agent  
2. Pick **harness** (only **available** ones allowed for start)  
3. Pick **model** / **provider** if that harness allows it  
4. Submit with start intent  
5. Desktop **spawns** ACP/harness child immediately  
6. Agent is online in their mesh/UI without a separate connect step  

If harness isn’t installed → create is blocked for start, or install flow from Settings first.

---

## How that differs from us

| | **Them** | **Us (today)** |
|---|---|---|
| Primary choice | **Harness** (local CLI/ACP) | **Location**: Built-in vs Remote |
| Built-in server agents | Not the main product loop | First-class (`builtin` + API keys) |
| Model picker | Driven by **harness + provider** | Driven by **runtime** Claude/Codex/Amp |
| Install/login | Settings harness catalog | Mostly outside the app |
| Come online | **Start** in app | Connect command **or** ACP Start (bolt-on) |
| Quit app | Agents killed | Same idea for ACP |

They fold “what runs my code” + “is it installed” + “which model” into **one harness-centric flow**. We split “where it runs” (Built-in/Remote) from “how it connects” (Connect dialog / ACP).

---

## What “configure them” means for them in one sentence

**Pick a harness that’s installed on this Mac, set model/provider for that harness, save, Start — the desktop app is the host.**

No Built-in/Remote toggle as the main control; no separate “pick Claude runtime then go generate a shell command” as the default path.

Done. Desktop ACP agents now **survive reboot** via app auto-start + restore.

### Behaviour

| Event | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Start on this Mac** | Saves agent + encrypted connect token; enables **Open at Login** |
| **Quit app** | Stops live processes (clean); list stays on disk |
| **Reboot / next launch** | App opens (login item) → after ~1.5s restores each saved agent (ACP spawn + WS register) |
| **Stop** | Removes from autostart (stays offline across reboot) |

### Storage
- Profile: `userData/acp-autostart.json` (ids, harness, workspace, baseUrl, …)
- Token: `acp-autostart.tokens` via **Electron `safeStorage`** (Keychain on macOS) — never plaintext `aga_` on disk
- If encryption isn’t available: profile saved, token not → restore asks for a re-Start

### Status UI
After Start you should see something like:  
`Grok on this Mac · auto-starts after reboot`

### Tests
`tests/desktop-acp-autostart.test.cjs` — 3/3 green (with bridge tests, 7 total)

### Caveats
1. **Desktop app must launch** after reboot (login item handles that when any agent is remembered).
2. **Backend must be reachable** (local `3142` or Fly) when restore runs.
3. **Re-minting** a connect token elsewhere invalidates the stored one → Start once more.
4. Don’t leave a **terminal `agensis connect`** on the same agent fighting the restored ACP session.

Restart Electron once so this code is loaded, then Start an agent and reboot to verify.

 do we have to make sure that we're connecting to fly fom local?

## Tools

- Lifecycle event

## Assistant

**No — not necessarily.** You only need Fly if you want the **same** agents/workspace as production web.

What matters is **one shared backend**, not Fly specifically.

| Setup | Desktop ACP | “Web” sees agent? |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop → **local `3142`**, browser → **agensis.io (Fly)** | Online only on local | **No** (different DB/WS) |
| Desktop → **local `3142`**, browser → **localhost:5173** (proxied to 3142) | Local | **Yes** |
| Desktop → **Fly**, browser → **agensis.io** | Production | **Yes** |

### What your logs show

Still **dev noise**, not “must use Fly”:

- `ws://127.0.0.1:5173/backend/ws` closed early → React Strict Mode unsub (renderer realtime)
- `version.json` 404 → update check in Vite dev
- GoTrue HTTP / Electron CSP → expected locally  

ACP bridge should hit **`ws://127.0.0.1:3142/backend/ws`** after our fix (not 5173). Confirm in **Electron main** terminal:  
`bridge start … ws=ws://127.0.0.1:3142/backend/ws`

### Practical rule

- **Dogfood only on this machine:** local backend is correct; don’t force Fly.  
- **See agents on https://agensis.io:** then **yes** — desktop (and ACP register) must use **Fly**, same as the site:

  - Set `VITE_BACKEND_BASE_URL=https://agensis-backend.fly.dev` for the desktop/renderer build/dev, **and**
  - ACP Start must register against that same base (token minted against Fly, not local 3142).

If the app is logged into **local** data but you open **production** web (or the reverse), agents will flash or never stick — wrong host, not ACP broken.

**Bottom line:** match backends. Local↔local or Fly↔Fly. Local desktop + Fly web will not share live agents.

## Assistant

**You already had autostart saved** — it just wasn’t restoring reliably.

### What’s on disk (your machine)

```
~/Library/Application Support/agensis/acp-autostart.json
  → Coder · harness claude · autoStart true · openAtLogin true

acp-autostart.tokens  (encrypted token present)
```

So **Start was persisting**. The gap was **restore on launch**.

### Why you still had to click Start

Most likely:

1. **Restore ran once after 1.5s** while **backend wasn’t ready** (or PATH wasn’t ready for GUI launch) → fail once, no retry.  
2. Restore treated “spawned” as success **without waiting for `agent_registered`** → looked dead in the UI.  
3. Cold PATH without a login-shell refresh → harness binary not found at restore.

### What we fixed

| Change | Effect |
|---|---|
| Refresh login-shell **PATH** before restore | Finds `claude` / adapters after reboot |
| **Retry** up to 6× (wait for `/backend/health`) | Backend lag after reboot |
| **Wait for `agent_registered`** | Only “ok” when server accepted the agent |
| Persist **before** bridge | Crash mid-register still restores next time |
| Louder main-process logs | See `restore begin/ok/failed` in Electron terminal |
| Don’t `unref` the restore timer | Restore isn’t dropped early |

### What you should do

1. **Fully quit and restart** Electron (`desktop:dev`).  
2. Watch the **main** process log (not only DevTools) for:
   ```
   [desktop-acp] restore (launch) pending=1
   [desktop-acp] restore ok agent=0d212ca9-…
   ```
3. Confirm **local backend is up** before/at launch (`3142` health) — restore will wait/retry, but Fly/local still must match where you saved `baseUrl`.

If restore logs `no token` or `backend not reachable`, paste that line. Your current files show the profile **is** remembered; the next launch should bring **Coder / Claude** back without a manual Start.

## Assistant

**Coder was connecting then dropping** because the desktop agent socket was racing itself. That’s fixed.

### What was going wrong

1. **Auth + register sent at the same time**  
   Server expects: auth frame → wait for settle → then `agent_register`.  
   We fired both immediately. That can yield a brief online row, then close / supersede / error.

2. **Reconnect opened a second socket without killing the first**  
   Two sockets for the same agent → server **supersedes** one → web shows connect → disconnect.

3. **Capabilities hash wrong**  
   We sent `capabilitiesHash` on sync; server stores **`hash`**. Heartbeats never matched → constant `agent_capabilities_refresh` (noisy; not always the drop, but fixed).

4. **Harness process death**  
   If `claude-code-acp` exited, the WS could linger or thrash. We now drop the bridge when the harness dies.

Your disk already had Coder saved (`harness: claude`, token encrypted). The unstable **wire** was the main issue.

### Fixes just applied

| Fix | Effect |
|---|---|
| Wait for `system/authenticated` before `agent_register` | Stable online |
| Generation + close prior socket on reconnect | No dual-socket supersede |
| Correct `hash` + answer `agent_capabilities_refresh` | Clean heartbeats |
| Heartbeat immediately + every 12s (no unref) | Stays “seen” |
| Harness exit → stop bridge | Honest offline |

### What you should do

1. **Fully quit Electron** and restart `desktop:dev` (must load new main process code).
2. **Stop any terminal** `agensis connect` for Coder (only one host).
3. **Start on this Mac** once for Coder (harness **Claude**).
4. Watch **Electron main** log for:
   ```
   [desktop-acp] authenticated agent=…
   [desktop-acp] registered agent=…
   ```
   **Not** a quick `ws close` right after.
5. Confirm it stays online for a few minutes; quit/relaunch and confirm restore without manual Start.

### Still required for “web + machine”

Web and desktop must use the **same backend** (both local `3142`, or both Fly). Local ACP + production web = different worlds.

If it still drops, paste the main-process lines around `authenticated` / `registered` / `ws close` / `agent_disabled` — that pinpoints the next failure.

## Assistant

**These are not ACP / agent errors.** They come from the in-app **Browser** window’s web proxy stack (Scramjet + bare-mux). Agents, connect tokens, and Fly are unrelated.

### What each line is

| Log | What it is |
|---|---|
| `bare-mux: running v2.1.9` | Proxy transport library starting (normal). |
| `failed to get a bare-mux SharedWorker MessagePort` | bare-mux’s SharedWorker handoff failed (Electron, multi-tab, or SW race). |
| `IDBDatabase … object stores was not found` | Scramjet’s `$scramjet` IndexedDB was created empty / at the wrong version — classic SW-vs-controller race. |
| `download-28.webp` 404 | Wallpaper asset requested under a **stale bare path**, not Vite’s hashed URL. |

### Scramjet / bare-mux (Browser panel)

On **web**, Browser uses Scramjet: backend fetches the page, SW rewrites it, bare-mux shuttles traffic.  
On **desktop Electron**, Browser uses `<webview>` and **should not load Scramjet at all**.

So if you see `scramjet.all.js` in the console, either:

1. You’re in a **normal browser tab** (not the Electron shell), or  
2. The Browser window fell back to the proxy path (`supportsWebviewTag()` was false).

The IDB error is already documented in `BrowserPanel.tsx`: the SW must not open `$scramjet` before `controller.init()`. A **leftover empty DB** from an earlier failed boot can still leave you broken until site data is cleared.

**If Browser is broken on web:** DevTools → Application → clear **IndexedDB** for this origin (especially `$scramjet`), unregister service workers, hard reload.  
**If you’re on desktop and only care about agents:** you can ignore these; they don’t affect ACP registration.

### `download-28.webp` 404

Wallpaper images are Vite-imported (`images/download-28.webp` → hashed `/assets/download-28-….webp`).  
`src/lib/backgrounds.ts` stores stable **ids** (`sunset-canyon`), not raw paths — precisely so old hashed paths don’t 404 after rebuild.

A stored `background_image` of `download-28.webp` or an old `/assets/download-28-….webp` will 404. Fix: pick the wallpaper again in Settings (or set a registry id). Cosmetic only — not agents.

### Bottom line

| Care about | Action |
|---|---|
| **ACP / Coder / agents** | Ignore this paste; different subsystem. |
| **In-app Browser on web** | Clear origin SW + `$scramjet` IDB, reload. |
| **Wallpaper missing** | Re-select background in Settings. |
| **Desktop Browser** | Should use webview — Scramjet noise usually means web, not Electron. |

If the Browser window is actually broken for you (blank page / won’t load sites), say whether that’s **desktop app** or **browser tab** and we can harden boot / clear the IDB race in code. If this was just console noise while debugging agents — you can drop it.

## Assistant

**Exactly 10s** matches this race, not ACP dying.

### What was happening

1. **Refresh** → bootstrap loads `agent_connections` from the DB with `status = online` (desktop wrote that to Neon).
2. **UI goes green** from that seed (no live-socket check).
3. **~seconds later** GET `/backend/agents/connections` (or the poll) **reconciles against sockets on this server process** via `isConnectionSocketLive`.
4. If the three ACP bridges are **not** on that same process, every row is forced **offline**.

Desktop can still look “connected” because local ACP (process + bridge IPC) is up on **this Mac**, while **web** only believes sockets attached to **the backend it is talking to**.

Shared Neon + split backends = classic false green, then honest offline.

### Fixes just landed

1. **Bootstrap** now uses the same live-socket reconcile as GET connections (no more optimistic green from DB alone).
2. **`useAgentConnections`** no longer lets a late bootstrap seed **overwrite** a correct offline fetch (that was the multi‑second green flash).

### What you should see now

| Setup | Web after refresh |
|---|---|
| Desktop ACP + web both on **local** `:3142` | Stay green if bridges are registered there |
| Desktop ACP on **local**, web on **agensis.io / Fly** | Stay **offline** (honest — sockets aren’t on Fly) |

Scramjet/bare-mux lines are still the **Browser** panel only — ignore for agents.

### To keep all three green on web

Point ACP at the **same** backend the browser uses:

- Local web (`localhost:5173` → `:3142`) → ACP `baseUrl` `http://127.0.0.1:3142` (what Start on this Mac should already mint when you’re on local).
- Production web (`agensis.io`) → ACP must register to **Fly** (`https://agensis-backend.fly.dev`), not only local.

Restart local server so the bootstrap change is live, hard-refresh web, and check again. If you want production web + local Mac agents, say so and we can wire desktop Start to always prefer the UI’s backend URL.

That hybrid setup is the whole story.

### What each side talks to

| Surface | Process | Backend it must use for “online” |
|---|---|---|
| **Live web** (agensis.io) | Browser | **Fly** only |
| **Local desktop** | Electron + ACP on your Mac | Bridge WS must be **Fly** if you want live web green |
| Local ACP harnesses | Claude/Codex/etc on disk | Stay on the Mac (that’s fine) |

“Online” is **not** “ACP process running.”  
It’s “this agent has an open WebSocket on the **same** backend the UI is using.”

So: **local process + Fly registration** = green on live web.  
**Local process + local `:3142` registration** = green on desktop/local only; live web will never stay green.

### What `desktop:dev` does today

`npm run desktop:dev` starts **local** Vite + **local** `:3142`.  
**Start on this Mac** mints a token and registers the bridge against that local API (or whatever `apiBaseUrl()` / mint `baseUrl` is).  
Live web never sees those sockets as live — which is the ~10s green-then-off you saw (DB row yes, Fly socket no).

### How to test live web + local desktop correctly

**Option A — desktop UI aimed at Fly (recommended for this test)**

1. Point the desktop renderer at the hosted backend:
   ```bash
   VITE_BACKEND_BASE_URL=https://agensis-backend.fly.dev npm run desktop:dev
   ```
   (Or use a packaged desktop build that already bakes Fly in.)
2. Sign in on desktop to the **same** workspace as live web.
3. **Stop** any ACP that was registered to `127.0.0.1:3142`.
4. **Start on this Mac** again for all three — mint + bridge should go to Fly (`wss://agensis-backend.fly.dev/backend/ws`).
5. Refresh **live web** → should stay green (not a 10s flash).

**Option B — keep desktop on local UI, only force ACP to Fly**

Possible but easy to misconfigure (local UI offline lights + Fly-only sockets). Prefer A for this test.


If you see `ws=ws://127.0.0.1:3142/...`, live web will not stay green.

## Assistant

**Yes — on a Mac, prod desktop build is supposed to sign** if your Developer ID cert is in the keychain. That’s intentional for shippable builds.

### What `desktop:build:prod` does

| Step | Expected |
|---|---|
| **Code sign** | Yes, if keychain has `Developer ID Application: Jason Kneen (SW75ZJJ5R6)` (from `package.json` `mac.identity`) |
| **Hardened runtime + entitlements** | Yes (`hardenedRuntime`, entitlements plists) |
| **Notarize** | Config says `notarize: true`, but full notary+staple is what **`npm run desktop:ship`** is for |
| **Verify** | Runs `desktop-verify-sign.mjs` after build (unless `SKIP_DESKTOP_SIGN_VERIFY=1`) |

`desktop:build.mjs` defaults `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=true` on mac so electron-builder finds that cert.

### What is *not* required for day-to-day

- **Unsigned local smoke:**  
  `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false SKIP_DESKTOP_SIGN_VERIFY=1 npm run desktop:build:local`  
  (or dist with the same env)
- **Ship to users:** signed **and** notarized → `npm run desktop:ship` (see `RELEASING.md`)

### How to tell it worked

```bash
codesign -dv --verbose=4 release/mac-arm64/agensis.app
# want: Authority=Developer ID Application: Jason Kneen (SW75ZJJ5R6)

npm run desktop:verify-sign
```

If you **don’t** have the cert, the build may still finish but as ad-hoc/unsigned, and verify-sign fails — that’s expected; not a “prod backend” thing, only a signing identity thing. **Prod** in the script name means **Fly backend URL**, not “always notarize.”

## Assistant

**Stop/Start when switching local ↔ prod:** expected once (new token + Fly `baseUrl`). After that, autostart should restore without you doing it again.

**“Finished without output” bug:** real bug, fixed.

### Cause
Streaming used `agent_job_delta` with `content` (correct).  
Finish used `agent_job_result` with **`content`**, but the server only reads **`response`** (classic daemon wire).

So the live stream looked fine, then finalize overwrote the bubble with:

`@coder finished without output.`

### Fix
1. **Desktop bridge** — send `response` (and `error`) on the final frame  
2. **Server** — accept `response` **or** `content`, and fall back to the last delta on the job row

### What you need
- **Restart desktop** (`desktop:dev:prod`) so the bridge fix loads  
- **Server fallback** only helps after **Fly deploy** of this commit; the bridge fix alone is enough for new turns

Then: Start ACP once if needed, send a message, stream should **stay** as the real answer when the turn ends.

## Assistant

**None of those block agents.** They’re expected noise under `desktop:dev:prod`.

| Log | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `[vite] connected` | HMR up | Good |
| React DevTools | Chrome suggestion | Ignore |
| **GoTrue HTTP** | Netlify Identity probes settings from `http://127.0.0.1:5173` | Dev-only. Production social login still uses HTTPS on agensis.io. Password/session login to Fly is fine. |
| **WS closed before established** | React Strict Mode: mount → unmount → remount; first socket is aborted | Harmless. Second connect should stick to `wss://agensis-backend.fly.dev/backend/ws` |
| Electron CSP `unsafe-eval` | Unpackaged Electron warning | Goes away when packaged |
| **`/version.json` 404** | Update check hits Vite origin; that file is only in prod builds | Expected in dev; not a real update failure |
| Forced reflow / handler 443ms | One-time cold paint cost | Ignore unless UI stays janky |

### What “healthy” looks like after this

- You’re signed in
- Agents green after **Start on this Mac** (bridge → Fly)
- Electron main log: `registered` with `wss://agensis-backend.fly.dev/...`
- Chat stream ends with real text (not “finished without output”) after the bridge fix + desktop restart

### Real problems (not in this paste)

- ACP still on `:3142` after switching to prod  
- “Finished without output” if desktop wasn’t restarted after the `response` field fix  
- Fly unreachable (auth/API hard fails)

**Verdict:** console is fine for desktop→Fly hotreload. Ignore this dump unless something is still broken in product behavior (agents offline, no stream, empty finish).

## Assistant

**Yes.** If desktop hosts the agent, the **agent’s model must be editable** as normal agent config — not locked because ACP is local.

### Product expectation

- **Harness** = which local runtime (Claude ACP / Codex ACP / Grok / …) — machine-local, Start dialog  
- **Model** = which model that agent uses for turns — **workspace agent setting**, same as remote daemon  

Users should be able to change model without rethinking “desktop vs CLI.” Change agent → save → (if already running) restart ACP so the new model applies.

### What we do today

| Piece | Today |
|---|---|
| Edit model on agent | Yes — create/edit form (`agent.model`) |
| Start ACP | Passes `model: agent.model \|\| 'auto'` into bridge |
| Register metadata | Advertises that model to the server |
| Start dialog | Harness only — **no model picker** (reads agent) |
| ACP child spawn | Harness args are fixed; **model is not yet forced into CLI flags** for most adapters |

So: **you can change the model on the agent**, and Start/autostart remember it. Full “ACP always runs *that* model” depends on each harness accepting model (e.g. Codex `--model`); that wiring is still incomplete for some adapters.

### Gap (if you want parity with a polished desktop host)

1. Show current model next to Start (and link “edit agent”).  
2. Optional model override in Start that writes back to `agent.model`.  
3. Pass model into harness spawn / ACP session when the adapter supports it.  
4. After model change while running → prompt Restart or restart bridge automatically.

**Bottom line:** Yes — they must let you change the model on that agent. We already store and pass it; we don’t yet fully drive every local harness with it or expose model in the Start flow. I can wire that next if you want.

ok so does buzz let you change the model in the chat prompt area?

## Tools

## Assistant

Checking what we know about Buzz’s chat model control and how ours compares.

## Tools

- WebSearch: Buzz AI desktop agent chat model selector prompt composer
- WebSearch: keyword(Buzz AI agent model picker OR "change model" desktop)
- Search: model.*composer|composer.*model|ModelSelect|selectedModel|AI_MODELS

## Assistant

**I don’t have a verified Buzz product dump** that proves their exact UI, so I won’t invent one. From how these products usually work (and how **agensis** is structured):

### Typical split

| Control | Who it applies to |
|---|---|
| **Composer model picker** | *Your* turn / generic AI chat (builtin / gateway / “talk to the workspace”) |
| **Agent model setting** | Turns that **that agent** runs (daemon / ACP / silo) |

For **agent-as-member** products (desktop hosts a local agent that registers as Coder, etc.), the model almost always lives on the **agent**, not as a free switch every message in the prompt bar. Changing model = edit agent (or agent settings), then next job uses it.

A **composer** model control for “this DM with Coder” is optional extra: per-thread or per-turn override. Some apps have it; many don’t, because the agent already owns runtime + model + permissions.

### What we do

- **Composer:** `ModelSelector` for human/workspace AI chat models  
- **Agent:** model on the agent form (`agent.model`), passed into desktop ACP Start as metadata  

Start-on-this-Mac picks **harness**, not model — model comes from the agent record.

### Practical answer

- **Must you be able to change the model for that agent?** **Yes** (agent config).  
- **Must that live in the chat prompt area?** **No** — only if you want per-chat/per-turn override; Buzz-like hosts usually put it on the agent, not the composer.

If you want parity either way: **(1)** clear model on agent edit (we have), or **(2)** composer override when the active session is an agent DM. Say which you want.

## Assistant

Looked at **`/Users/jkneen/Documents/GitHub/buzz`**. Here’s what the code actually does.

### Chat prompt area — **no**

`MessageComposer` / `MessageComposerToolbar` are attach, format, mention, send. **No model control** in the composer.

### Where Buzz **does** change model

| Surface | What |
|---|---|
| **Agent create / edit** (`AgentDefinitionDialog`, `AgentInstanceEditDialog`) | Provider + **model** dropdown (persona / instance config) |
| **Agent config panel** (`AgentConfigFields`, defaults) | Global / agent default model |
| **`ModelPicker.tsx`** | Compact dropdown on a **managed agent**: list models from the harness, persist default, or live `switch_model` while the agent has active turns |

That picker is **agent-scoped**, not “this message in the composer.” Live path only when:

- persona-linked agent  
- status running/deployed  
- **at least one active turn** → `switch_model` per channel; otherwise it saves the agent default and may show **“restart to apply”**

Note: `ModelPicker` is implemented (and wired to `switchManagedAgentModel` / control results), but **nothing in the tree currently `import`s it** — only edit dialogs use the fuller model selects. So the *design* is agent-level (+ optional live switch), not composer-level; the compact picker may be mid-rollout / unused in this checkout.

### Bottom line (from Buzz source)

- **Not** “change model in the chat prompt bar” like generic ChatGPT.  
- **Yes** — change model on the **agent** (settings / instance edit).  
- Optional **live switch** for a running agent mid-session, not a free human-composer model.

For agensis, matching Buzz means: solid **agent model** control (we have the field) + optional live/restart apply for desktop ACP — **not** stuffing agent model into the channel composer next to send.

## Assistant

Implemented the Buzz-style **agent model picker** (not a chat-composer control).

### What Buzz does (from their source)
- Model lives on the **agent**, not in `MessageComposer`
- Compact dropdown on the agent surface
- Persist default; if running → **restart to apply** (live `switch_model` is their mid-turn path; we restart ACP)

### What we shipped

1. **`AgentModelPicker`** (`src/components/agents/AgentModelPicker.tsx`)  
   - Pill dropdown, models from `modelOptionsForRuntime`  
   - Saves `agent.model`  
   - If ACP is running → **Restart to apply** (re-mint + re-Start with new model)

2. **Agent details** — model badge → live picker  

3. **Connect → This Mac** — harness + model picker side by side  

4. **ACP host** — passes model into env (`CODEX_MODEL` / `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` / `AGENSIS_AGENT_MODEL`) on spawn  

### How to use
1. Open agent → change model on the pill  
2. If ACP is running, click **Restart to apply**  
3. Or stop/start from Connect after changing model  

Composer **human** model selector is unchanged — same as Buzz (agent model ≠ chat-composer model).

## Assistant

**Right — Hermes was being mislabeled.**

The form only knew classic pins (**Claude / Codex / Amp**). Empty pin defaulted to **Claude**, so a Hermes ACP agent showed “Claude — ready” + Claude models. That’s wrong.

### Fix

| Runtime choice | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Claude / Codex / Amp | Server pin (`metadata.runtime`) — classic daemon |
| **Desktop ACP** | **No pin** — Hermes, Grok, Goose, Claude ACP, etc. |

- Empty / missing pin → **Desktop ACP** (not Claude)
- Saving Desktop ACP **clears** `metadata.runtime` so the server won’t demand Claude
- Model for Desktop ACP → freeform + “Harness default” (not Claude-only list)

### What you should do for Hermes

1. Edit Hermes  
2. Runtime → **Desktop ACP — no pin · any local harness**  
3. Model → **Harness default** (or a freeform id Hermes understands)  
4. **Save**  
5. Connect → harness **Hermes** → Start  

You should **not** see “Claude — ready” for that agent anymore.

## Assistant

**Same root cause as Hermes.** Grok is a **Desktop ACP harness**, but this agent was saved as **Remote + Claude** (the old default). The form is showing what’s in the DB, not the harness you pick on Start.

### Why it shows “Claude — ready”
Create/edit used to default daemon agents to `metadata.runtime = claude`.  
Connect → harness **Grok** is separate. The bar still shows the **server pin**, so you get Claude models (Opus 5) that don’t match Grok.

### Fix this Grok agent (once)
1. Edit Grok  
2. Runtime → **Desktop ACP — no pin · any local harness** (now first in the list)  
3. Model → **Harness default** (or freeform)  
4. **Save**  
5. Connect → Grok → Start  

After that it must not say Claude.

### What we changed so new ones don’t do this
- **Desktop ACP** is first in the runtime list  
- On Electron, new **Remote** agents default to **Desktop ACP**, not Claude  
- Switching an edit form to Remote on desktop also jumps to Desktop ACP  

**Keep** Claude/Codex/Amp only when you really want a classic server pin for that runtime.

## Assistant

**Short answer:** yes, one setting still matters for routing; most of the rest is noise once you’re on ACP. And if the form says **Built-in** while ACP is green, ACP is **not** the thing answering turns.

### How work actually routes

When someone @mentions an agent, the server picks a lane from `run_mode` (and one special case):

| Setting | What runs the turn |
|--------|---------------------|
| **Built-in** | Fly server, in-process model call. **Ignores** desktop ACP and the CLI daemon. |
| **Remote** (`daemon`) | A live WebSocket worker gets `agent_job` — either **desktop ACP** or **`agensis-agent` CLI**. Same lane. |
| **MCP / external** | Pull queue (`claim_job`). Only if an MCP client is present as that agent. |

Desktop ACP and the agensis CLI are **not two products**. They’re two ways to attach the same **Remote** worker:

- Desktop ACP = Electron hosts Hermes/Grok/Claude Code/… and bridges to the backend  
- CLI = `agensis-agent connect` on a machine  
- Both register, both go green, both can serve **web + desktop** if they hit the same Fly backend  

So for “ACP serves the web,” the agent must be **Remote**, not Built-in.

### What you still need vs what you don’t

**Still load-bearing**

1. **Built-in vs Remote**  
   - Built-in = works with no laptop, uses workspace/server model  
   - Remote = must have a live connection (ACP or CLI) or the turn fails with “no daemon connected”

2. **Which machine is connected** (implicit)  
   Green connection = that process can take jobs. No connection + Remote = offline for work.

**Mostly preference / cleanup (not a second engine)**

- **Classic runtime pin** (`claude` / `codex` / `amp`) — only for old daemon enforcement  
- **`acp_harness`** — which local harness to Start (Hermes vs Grok vs …), not a separate server mode  
- Separate “desktop ACP vs CLI” product flag — **not needed**; same daemon path  

### Your “Built-in but using ACP” case

That’s inconsistent with the code path:

- Built-in → server answers  
- ACP green → connection is registered and shows online  
- **Jobs do not go to ACP while `run_mode` is Built-in**

So either:

- turns still feel “agent-like” because **Built-in** is answering (server Claude), while ACP is only a green light, or  
- some agents are actually Remote and others Built-in  

For ACP (or CLI) to own the work: set those agents to **Remote**, Start ACP (or run the CLI), leave them online.

### Do we still need all those agent settings?

**Product-wise, you can shrink the UI a lot** without removing the underlying switch:

| Keep (or auto-set) | Drop / hide for most people |
|--------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Where work runs:** This Mac (ACP/CLI) vs Server (Built-in) vs MCP client | Manual Claude/Codex/Amp pins on desktop |
| Preferred **ACP harness** when on This Mac | Separate “desktop vs CLI” modes |
| Model (when the harness cares) | Treating Built-in + ACP as the same thing |

Reasonable defaults:

- **Start ACP / Connect CLI** → force or offer **Remote** and clear classic pins  
- **Stop all workers and want server-only** → Built-in  
- Don’t make people pick Claude runtime if the real choice is Hermes/Grok ACP  

### Bottom line

- You do **not** need a third mode for “desktop ACP vs CLI” — one Remote path covers both and can serve the web.  
- You **do** still need Built-in vs Remote (and MCP when that’s the client).  
- Agents set to **Built-in while ACP is running are misconfigured for ACP work** — flip them to **Remote** if you want Hermes/Grok/CLI to answer.

If you want, next step is a small product fix: **when ACP starts (or CLI connects), auto-set `run_mode` to `daemon` and stamp `acp_harness`**, so the form can’t say Built-in while the green light is ACP.

## Assistant

Yes — the current labels fight the mental model.

### What’s actually true

| Code | What happens | User-facing truth |
|------|----------------|-------------------|
| `builtin` | Turn runs **on the agensis backend** (Fly), with server/workspace models | No laptop required |
| `daemon` | Turn is pushed to a **live socket** | Desktop ACP **or** `agensis-agent` CLI — same path |
| `external` | MCP client pulls jobs | Third-party client *is* the agent |

So **“Remote” is server jargon** (“not in-process”). From the human’s view, desktop ACP is **local**, and the CLI might be their laptop *or* another machine. Calling both “Remote” is what feels wrong.

### Better naming

Think in terms of **where the brain runs**, not “builtin vs remote”:

| Mode | Good label | Subtitle / help |
|------|------------|------------------|
| `builtin` | **Hosted** (or **On agensis**) | Runs on agensis servers. Works even if this Mac is closed. |
| `daemon` | **Connected** (or **On a host**) | Runs on a machine that’s online as this agent — desktop app or CLI. |
| `external` | **MCP client** (keep) | An external app answers as this agent. |

**Builtin → best called “Hosted”** (or “On agensis”).

Why not:

- **Built-in** — sounds like a feature pack, not a place of execution  
- **Cloud** — true-ish, but people load it with “ChatGPT cloud” baggage  
- **Server** — accurate for engineers, cold for product  
- **Default** — lies; it’s one option, not always the default for coding agents  

**Hosted** / **On agensis** = “agensis runs it for you.”

**Daemon → best not called “Remote”.**

Prefer:

- **Connected** — matches the green light and Connect flow  
- or **On a host** — covers desktop *and* CLI without saying “your Mac only”

Then under Connect, split the *how*, not a second mode:

- **This Mac (ACP)** — Electron starts Hermes/Grok/…  
- **Any machine (CLI)** — `agensis-agent connect`  

Same `run_mode = daemon`. Different attach methods.

### Suggested UI shape

```
Where does this agent run?
○ Hosted          — on agensis, no machine needed
○ Connected       — on a linked host (desktop ACP or CLI)
○ MCP client      — external app claims jobs
```

When **Connected** is selected, secondary line (not a third run mode):

```
Link:  [ Start on this Mac (ACP) ]  [ CLI command… ]
Harness: Hermes Agent — ready
```

### Short answers

- **Remote** today = desktop ACP **or** agensis daemon CLI — correct technically, bad word.  
- **Builtin** is best renamed **Hosted** (or **On agensis**).  
- You do **not** need two top-level modes for desktop vs CLI — one **Connected** mode + two link methods.

I can rename the form labels (`Built-in` → `Hosted`, `Remote` → `Connected`) and the help copy in one pass if you want that next.

## Assistant

The shape is good: **three places work can run**, not “builtin vs remote.” Mapping and a few sharp edges:

### Your proposal vs the real lanes

| Your term | Maps to | Accurate? |
|-----------|---------|-----------|
| **Direct** | `builtin` — turn on agensis, model via server/workspace key (or gateway) | Yes for “no linked host” |
| **Relay** | `daemon` — job pushed to desktop ACP **or** CLI | Yes — best of the three names |
| **Connector** | MCP as the agent; maybe other attach surfaces | Partly — don’t dump webhooks in the same bucket without care |

### What works

- **Relay** is the strongest word. Server doesn’t run the brain; it **forwards** the turn to a live host. Desktop and CLI are both relays. That kills the “remote vs local” confusion.
- Three buckets match the product: hosted / linked host / external client.
- **Connector** fits **MCP** well (“something external is plugged in as this agent”).

### Where it stretches

**1. Direct**

- Honest meaning: *agensis calls the model for you* (hosted completion).
- Risk: people hear “direct API key” and think *their* key on *their* machine. Builtin is usually **agensis’s / workspace key on the server**, not “I pasted OpenAI into this Mac.”
- Desktop Grok/Claude with *local* login is **Relay**, not Direct — even though a key is involved.

So: **Direct = hosted by agensis**, not “any path that uses an API key.”

Better subtitles:

- **Direct** — *Runs on agensis. Uses workspace / hosted model access.*
- Not: *“API key direct to provider”* as the main definition (too easy to mix with local harness auth).

**2. Connector + webhooks**

- **MCP** = something acts *as* the agent (pull jobs / register).
- **Webhooks** = something *wakes* an agent (inbound trigger), still needs Direct or Relay to answer.
- Putting both under **Connector** without a split will re-confuse people.

Safer:

- **Connector** = MCP (and similar “client is the agent”)
- Webhooks stay under Connect as *triggers*, not a third execution home — or a sub-line under Connector later if you really want one surface

**3. Farm / other**

Anything that is still “live socket gets `agent_job`” stays **Relay**, even if it’s not desktop.

### Tightened version

| Label | One-line | Includes |
|-------|----------|----------|
| **Direct** | Agensis runs the turn itself | Server/builtin, hosted models / gateways |
| **Relay** | Agensis hands the turn to a linked host | Desktop ACP, `agensis-agent` CLI, same wire |
| **Connector** | An external client is the agent | MCP (not webhooks as the mode) |

Optional microcopy under Relay:

> Desktop app or CLI — same path; web and desktop both see it when it’s online.

### Vs Hosted / Connected

| | Direct / Relay / Connector | Hosted / Connected / MCP |
|--|---------------------------|---------------------------|
| Metaphor | How the turn is delivered | Where it runs |
| Best for | People who think in integrations | People who think in machines |
| Weakness | “Direct” needs a careful subtitle | “Connected” is softer, less clever |

**Relay** is better than **Connected**.  
**Direct** is fine if the subtitle is “on agensis,” not “your API key.”  
**Connector** is fine if it means **MCP identity**, not “every pipe into the product.”

### Recommendation

Ship the triad as:

- **Direct** — runs on agensis  
- **Relay** — desktop or daemon host  
- **Connector** — MCP client  

Keep harness (Hermes/Grok/…) as a **Relay detail**, not a fourth mode.  
Keep webhooks as **how you wake** an agent, not a peer of Direct/Relay/Connector.

If you want this in the UI next, the rename is mostly copy + the form select (`builtin` / `daemon` / `external` stay in code). I can do that pass when you say go.

## Assistant

Correct.

**Relay** is one *routing* path (agensis pushes jobs to a linked host). There are two *local* ways to run those jobs:

| How you attach | Protocol on the machine | Package / surface |
|----------------|-------------------------|-------------------|
| **Desktop → Start on this Mac** | **ACP** (stdio to Hermes / Grok / Claude Code ACP / …) | Electron `electron/acp/*` — not the npm daemon |
| **`agensis connect` (CLI)** | **Not ACP** — spawns `claude` / `codex` / Amp etc. as a normal CLI | `@agensis/agensis-agent` |

So:

- **`@agensis/agensis-agent@0.1.47`** = classic Relay CLI. WebSocket to agensis → job → coding CLI. **No ACP.**
- **Desktop ACP** = same Relay *job path* on the server, different local runner (ACP adapters).

Same product mode (**Relay**), different machine-side implementation. Connector (MCP) is a third path again.

## User

ok so what happens if we update the CLI and publish it for existing users -- can the original connect strings still work?

## Tools

- Lifecycle event

## Assistant

**Yes — upgrading the CLI does not invalidate old connect strings.**

### What still works

An existing line like:

```sh
agensis connect \
  --url https://… \
  --token aga_… \
  --workspace … \
  --agent … \
  --handle … \
  --model … \
  --permission-mode …
```

keeps working after:

```sh
npm i -g @agensis/agensis-agent@latest   # e.g. 0.1.47
```

or `npx @agensis/agensis-agent@latest …` with the **same** flags.

Reason:

| Piece | Unchanged by 0.1.47 rename/docs |
|--------|----------------------------------|
| Flag names (`--url`, `--token`, …) | same |
| Token shape (`aga_…`) | same |
| WS path / register / job / delta / result | same |
| Server `run_mode: 'daemon'` (Relay) | same wire value |

The Direct / Relay / Connector work was **product language + app UI**, not a new connect protocol. The published package is still the same Relay CLI host under a clearer description.

### What does *not* survive (and never did)

1. **Minting a new connect command in the app**  
   That **rotates** the agent’s connect token and sets Relay. Any **old** string that still has the **previous** `aga_…` will fail auth until you use the new command (or re-save the profile with the new token).

2. **Saved profiles**  
   Profiles that stored the old token keep working until you mint/rotate. After rotation, update the profile / re-run setup with the new command.

3. **Pinning an ancient package on purpose**  
   `npx @agensis/agensis-agent@0.1.xx connect …` still uses that old binary + the same string; only if that old version is gone from npm or the server later requires a newer protocol would it break. Normal `@latest` upgrade is fine.

### Practical guidance for existing users

- Upgrade CLI: **safe**; keep running the same command if the token is still current.  
- After someone hits **Connect → generate command** again: **must** replace the old command/token everywhere (CLI service, profile, cron).  
- Desktop ACP is separate; CLI upgrade doesn’t change ACP sessions.

**Short answer:** original connect strings keep working across a CLI publish as long as you don’t rotate the token. Upgrading npm alone is not a reconnect tax.

## User

ok and older non-upgraded CLIs in the interim will still work?

## Tools

- Lifecycle event

## Assistant

**Yes.** Older CLIs that were never upgraded keep working against the current backend while others move to `@latest`.

### Why

Nothing in this release **required** a new client protocol:

- Same WebSocket auth + register / heartbeat / job / delta / result  
- Same `aga_…` connect tokens  
- Same flags on `agensis connect …`  
- Same server `run_mode: 'daemon'` (Relay is only a label)

So a machine still on e.g. `0.1.40` and one on `0.1.47` can both stay online on the same workspace.

### What *can* stop an old CLI (not the rename)

| Cause | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| **Token rotated** (new connect command / mint) | Old string fails; re-run with new token |
| **Agent set to Direct** | No Relay host is used for turns; green CLI may be irrelevant |
| **Very old CLI + classic runtime pin** (e.g. Amp) | Server may refuse if the client doesn’t declare runtime (existing rule, not new) |
| **Future** server change that raises min protocol | Would be intentional; not this interim |

### Interim ops

- Safe mixed fleet: upgraded and non-upgraded CLIs side by side  
- No need to force-upgrade just because of Direct / Relay / Connector naming  
- Upgrade when you want the new package docs/fixes; not to stay online after this change  

**Bottom line:** non-upgraded CLIs still work in the interim; only token rotation or unrelated protocol/pin rules break them, not the new product language or the 0.1.47 publish.

**No.** The new CLI (`@agensis/agensis-agent@0.1.47`) does **not** switch to ACP.

### Current split (unchanged by this release)

| Attach path | Protocol on the machine |
|-------------|-------------------------|
| **Desktop → Start on this Mac** | **ACP** (stdio to Hermes / Grok / Claude Code ACP / …) |
| **CLI `agensis connect`** | **Not ACP** — spawns `claude` / `codex` / Amp etc. as normal processes |

`0.1.47` only aligned naming/docs (Relay host) and shipped that package. Wire + local execution for the CLI are still the classic daemon path.

### So for users

- New CLI = still **Relay via CLI subprocesses**, not ACP  
- Old CLI = same  
- ACP = still **desktop app only** (plus any future host that implements ACP)

If you want the **CLI** to become an ACP host (spawn ACP adapters like desktop does), that’s a separate feature — not what shipped. I can outline or implement that if you want it next.

| ACP harness on PATH (claude-agent-acp, codex-acp, hermes, grok, …) | **ACP** (same idea as desktop) |
| No harness / ACP init fails | **Classic** SDK / subprocess |
| `--no-acp` or `AGENSIS_ACP=0` | Always classic |

Harness pick order: `metadata.acp_harness` → `--acp-harness` → `--runtime` / coding family.

### Compatibility

- Old connect strings still work  
- Old CLIs still work  
- New CLI can use **both** ACP and classic  

### Tests

- Integration: **183 pass** (suite runs with `AGENSIS_ACP=0` so adapters on PATH don’t hang CI)  
- Unit: **245 pass**  
- Build + pack smoke: pass

## Assistant

Those screenshots are **Cursor’s Custom Connector** (or the same ChatGPT-style connector UI), not our Connect Flows dialog. What’s going on:

### What that form expects
After Name + Server URL (`…/sse`), the client decides the server needs **OAuth 2.1** and asks for:

| Field | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| Client ID | OAuth app / registered client |
| Client Secret | Optional (often empty with PKCE) |
| Authorization endpoint | `…/authorize` |
| Token endpoint | `…/token` |
| Scopes | Space-separated OAuth scopes |
| Token auth method | `none` (PKCE) / `client_secret_post` / `client_secret_basic` |

### What agensis has today
**Bearer tokens only** — not OAuth.

| Surface | What it gives |
|---------|----------------|
| Settings → workspace MCP credential | Endpoint `POST …/backend/mcp` + `agw_…` bearer |
| Connect Flows | Same MCP door + optional **signed webhook** for Flows events |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP JSON-RPC, **not** a dedicated SSE OAuth MCP server |

There is **no** `/authorize`, `/token`, Dynamic Client Registration, or Protected Resource Metadata. So putting “Client ID / Authorization Endpoint / Scopes” into Connect Flows **without a real OAuth server** would just give people values that Cursor’s OAuth form can’t successfully use.

Connect Flows is also the wrong product home: it’s for **Flows webhooks + MCP**, not “paste into Cursor Custom Connector.”

### What works in Cursor **right now**
Skip Custom Connector OAuth. Use Tools & MCP / `mcp.json` with the credential we already mint:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agensis": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://agensis-backend.fly.dev/backend/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer agw_…"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

(or the `claude mcp add --transport http … --header "Authorization: Bearer …"` line we already show).

### What “add these values in settings” actually means
Two different product choices:

1. **Docs/UI only** — In MCP settings, show a **“Cursor / Custom Connector”** panel that says: *Custom Connector OAuth isn’t supported yet; use bearer `mcp.json` like above.* Optional: copyable Server URL + token only. **Does not make that OAuth form work.**

2. **Real MCP OAuth (makes that form work)** — Implement an OAuth AS for the MCP door, then surface copy fields in **MCP settings** (not Connect Flows):
   - Server URL (HTTP MCP; SSE only if we add it)
   - Client ID (+ optional secret)
   - Authorization / token endpoints
   - Recommended scopes + token auth method (`none` + PKCE)
   - Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (+ protected-resource metadata)

That’s a real backend feature (authorize UI, code→token, map token → workspace/agent MCP identity, PKCE, redirect allowlist for Cursor).

---

**Recommendation:** Don’t bolt OAuth fields onto Connect Flows. Either:

- **A)** Ship clearer MCP settings copy + Cursor bearer recipe (small, honest), or  
- **B)** Implement MCP OAuth properly, then show those fields under MCP settings.

Which do you want next — **A (docs/settings only)** or **B (full OAuth so Custom Connector works)**?

## Assistant

**Done.** Connections is now a real status surface, not a “click Generate then maybe see something” dead end. “Flows” is gone from the UI.

### What you get in **Settings → Connections**
Opens and **immediately** loads:

| Field | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| **Status badge** | Credential issued / No credential yet |
| **Endpoint** | Always visible + copy |
| **`claude mcp add`** | Always visible (placeholder token in the command) + copy |
| **Bearer token** | Show/hide eye + copy **only after Issue/Rotate this session** |
| If already issued | “Issued earlier… Rotate to mint a new one” (hash-only at rest — we cannot re-show an old token) |
| **Auto-approve** | Toggle on load |
| **Issue / Rotate** | Mints once; rotate invalidates the previous credential |
| **Refresh status** | Re-fetch without rotating |

### Naming
| Old | New |
|-----|-----|
| Connect Flows | **Event webhooks** |
| Generate workspace control credential | **MCP connection** + **Issue / Rotate credential** |
| Channel menu “Connect” | **Event webhook** |

### Backend
- `GET /backend/workspaces/:id/mcp-connection` — owner-only status, **no secret**
- `POST …/mcp-token` still returns the live token **once** on mint/rotate
- Netlify allowlist updated for the new GET

### Why the token isn’t always on screen
Only a **hash** is stored. Showing a token every time would mean either re-minting on every open (breaks existing clients) or storing plaintext (security regression). So: **endpoint always; secret only right after Issue/Rotate**, with hide/show.

Tests: workspace MCP owner + unit flowConnect green; typecheck clean.
